The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused Mohd. Hasin is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Chicken Plaza, from where the food article, that is, 'Haldi Powder' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 26.07.2004, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) Shyam Lal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. N.R.Sharma reached along with their staff at M/s. Chicken Plaza at 5034, Netaji Subhash Marg, Darya Ganj Delhi, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, including Haldi Powder which was lying stored for use in preparation of other food articles meant for sale for human consumption, as lying in an open container bearing no label declaration. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Haldi Powder from the vendor, to which he agreed. One Constable Kamal Singh was also joined as a witness. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per "34. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 10.08.2004, the PA found the sample to be adulterated because it was coloured with unpermitted synthetic colouring matter viz Metanil yellow and also because it contained foreign starch. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by the FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 21.12.2004 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a), (b), (c), (f), (h), (j), (l) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 21.12.2004. The accused appeared and filed an application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample analysed from the Central Food Laboratory (CFL). The application was allowed and a counterpart was sent for analysis to CFL. The CFL examined the sample and its Director gave Certificate dated 24.03.2005, opining the sample to be not conforming to the standards of turmeric (Haldi) powder due to presence of non-permitted red and orange oil soluble synthetic colours and also due to presence of rice starch in abundance with turmeric structure. 4. On the basis of CFL Report, the matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 FI Shyam Lal. On the basis of his deposition, charge was framed against the accused on 31.07.2010 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) PFA Act, being violation of sections 2(ia)(a), (b), (j) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. At the trial, the witness examined in pre-charge stage of evidence was recalled for cross- examination in post-charge stage and additionally, prosecution examined PW-2 Sh. N.R.Sharma (SDM/LHA) and PW-3 HC Kamal Singh in post- charge stage. 5. PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. PW-3, a police official, was returning to his home when he was joined as a witness by the food officials. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 26.07.2004 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 750 gms of Haldi Powder after homogenizing it with the help of a clean and dry spoon, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, fastening, sealing and marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that different samples were sent to different analysts, or that representative sample was not taken or that some yellow colour was sticking to the cloth / hands / sample bottles used in the sample proceedings. 6.
